history.summary: A small Surya (sun) temple at Sector 4F, Sector 4, Bokaro Steel City (address listings: Sector 4-F, Bokaro 827004; geocoded as 'Surya Mandir-Sun Temple, Block G, Sector-4'). It appears only in business/temple directories (Justdial: 4.2 rating from 325 ratings) with no published history, founding date, trust details or festival programme — sourcing is THIN and the entry is largely a placeholder pending local verification. A YouTube city tour of Bokaro places it in the same Sector 4 cluster as the Jagannath Temple (Sector 4D). CAUTION: the name is generic — do not confuse with the famous Surya Mandirs of Jamshedpur (Sidgora), Bundu (Ranchi) or Baghmara, which are separate temples in other towns.

town_description: Bokaro Steel City is a planned industrial city in Bokaro district, Jharkhand, built around the Bokaro Steel Plant — one of India's first public-sector steel plants, commissioned in the 1960s with Soviet collaboration. The city is laid out in numbered sectors with broad avenues, parks and markets, and draws settlers from across India, which is reflected in its temples representing many regional traditions. Nearby attractions include Garga Dam, the Parasnath Hills (a major Jain pilgrimage site) and the Rajrappa Chhinnamasta temple.
